posts.note: Satirical story told by a far-future narrator about the October 2025 AWS outage. One implied climate joke logged with sincere=false; the other jokes (sharks as pets, pumpkins) have no sincere underlying claim and were not logged.

Republished 2022 article in first-person plural voice on media guidelines for suicide reporting. One hope-framed call about improving coverage logged; advice to readers and the closing sharing wish not logged.
Halloween essay on emotional vampires and AI chatbots. One quoted third-party energy forecast logged (own_claim=false). Present-tense claims about chatbots crowding out human interaction not logged.

Guest analysis by reader 'Dr. MS' of the KARMA-Dep 2 ketamine vs midazolam trial, framed by Owen Muir. One guest sales call about Janssen logged (own_claim=false). Owen's own closing efficacy belief about Spravato and ketamine is present-tense and was not logged.
Advice essay on latitude, sunlight and suicide risk in bipolar disorder. Conditional individual-level advice ('the more stable your life may become') has no world-state forecast; nothing logged.
113-word pointer to a Carlat Psychiatry Podcast appearance on TMS; no forward-looking claims.

Conference rant on adolescent depression treatments. Four calls logged (youth suicide attempt rate this year, chatbots and drugs won't fix the crisis, permanent workforce shortage, accelerated TMS might work). 'We should pay for that, routinely, and first line' is normative with no predictive reading and was not logged.

Post on the day of the FDA clearance of Brainsway deep TMS (H1 coil) for adolescent depression. One adoption call logged. The restated earlier opinion that brain stimulation is likely an appropriate adolescent treatment is past analysis at post date and was not logged.

Round-up of the author's outside writing. One RAMHT event date logged. The Everyday Health headline 'Could Lead to More Personalized Prescribing' is a third-party title the author does not adopt; the MedCity quote is normative. Neither logged.

CNS Summit panel prep on GLP-1 drugs and suicide risk. One call about more GLP-1 drugs coming soon logged. The conclusion that GLP-1s do not cause suicide is a present-evidence claim; the EMA probe sentence is past tense. Neither logged.
102-word post cut short by an internet outage. A future-tense prevalence statistic and a joke expectation that the internet recovers quickly are both logged as borderline.
Podcast post on a phase 3 trial of cTBS for auditory hallucinations. Only the RAMHT 2026 SF event announcement logged.

Review of the AJP DBT vs SSRI trial in BPD. Only the RAMHT event note logged. 'Should extend the black box warning to BPD?', 'we need more robust reimbursement', 'psychiatrists should consider never prescribing prozac', 'Health plans? Update your prior authorization standards' and 'I hope this data blocks the use of SSRIs' are normative or wishes with no predictive reading and were not logged.
Personal essay on grief plus a Kendler-group suicide prediction study. Truisms ('you're gonna be working with people who die') and the Time Machine joke not logged.
Holiday conversation guide. 'Politics will come up' and 'Mental health will, reliably, come up' are truisms about family dinners and were not logged.

statements.quote: It was the middle of October— yes, back when October used to be a cold month!
statements.context: Opening of a satirical story told by a narrator in a distant future, recounting the October 2025 AWS outage. The aside implies that in the future October is no longer a cold month, a climate joke.
statements.note: Satirical far-future frame; implied warming-climate claim does not read as a real forecast. Logged for recall only.

statements.quote: I certainly hope that is changing and that coverage will continue to improve when suicides do occur.
statements.context: Republished 2022 article on how media report on suicide. Journalists told the author they got little training on suicide reporting; the author hopes that training is changing and that media coverage will keep improving after future suicide deaths.
statements.note: Hope framing; borderline wish. Article dates to 2022 and is written in first-person plural; republished 2025-10-25.

statements.quote: That demand from AI , the research states, could double by the end of this year, comprising nearly half of all total data-center electricity consumption worldwide, excluding the electricity used for bitcoin mining.
statements.context: In an essay comparing AI chatbots to emotional vampires, the author quotes a news report on research published in the journal Joule: AI power demand, already up to 20 percent of global data-center demand, could double by year end.
statements.horizon_text: by the end of this year
statements.note: Quoted third-party forecast (Joule research via a news report). The author cites it in support but does not restate it as his own.

statements.quote: This is why Janssen, the manufacturer, is still making huge profits from a simple enantiomer—on track for $2b this year.
statements.context: Guest section by a reader, 'Dr. MS', a psychiatrist with bipolar disorder, analyzing the KARMA-Dep 2 ketamine vs midazolam trial (JAMA Psychiatry). He argues IV ketamine beats intranasal esketamine but is generic, so Janssen keeps profiting from Spravato, which he says is on track for $2 billion in sales in 2025.
statements.note: Guest author Dr. MS, not Owen Muir. Owen introduces and thanks him but does not adopt this sales claim.

statements.quote: 13% of high school girls will attempt suicide. 7% of high school boys will attempt suicide. That's in 2023. I doubt it it's better this year.
statements.context: Opening of a rant, written from a conference, on adolescent depression treatments. The author cites 2023 figures for high-school suicide attempts and doubts that the 2025 figures are better.
statements.note: Call about the 2025 youth suicide-attempt rate relative to the cited 2023 figures.

statements.quote: We're not gonna fix that with a chat bot. We're not gonna fix that with drugs, because, as you'll remember me telling you, the largest data sets tell us they don't work.
statements.context: Same rant on the youth mental health crisis. The author denies that chatbots or oral antidepressant drugs will fix high adolescent suicide-attempt rates, on the grounds that large data sets show the drugs do not work.
statements.note: Negative call about two intervention classes (chatbots, antidepressant drugs); compound claim.

statements.quote: There will never be enough of those Therapists. There will absolutely never be enough child Psychiatrists.
statements.context: Same rant. The author says psychotherapy works for adolescent depression but requires humans and training, then predicts a permanent shortage of therapists and of child psychiatrists.
statements.note: Workforce forecast; compound claim (therapists and child psychiatrists).

statements.quote: You know what might work? Accelerated transcranial magnetic stimulation.
statements.context: Same rant. After listing oral antidepressants he says do not work for adolescent depression, the author proposes accelerated TMS as the treatment that might work, notes once-daily TMS already has an FDA label, and urges running studies on accelerated protocols because rapid designs make group differences easier to detect.
statements.note: Hedged efficacy call ahead of trial evidence; paired with 'We should run to the studies on accelerated transcranial magnetic stimulation'.

statements.quote: Now, more kids will get more effective treatment for their depression.
statements.context: Post dated 2025-11-14, the day the FDA cleared the Brainsway H1 coil (deep TMS) for adolescent depression, about a year after Neuronetics got the first adolescent TMS label. The author thanks patients who paid out of pocket before the label and predicts more adolescents will now receive more effective depression treatment.
statements.note: Author's employer Radial provides deep TMS; coder may consider CONTROL.

statements.quote: the next one is coming up on January 11th, 2026!
statements.context: The author describes his live newsletter event series RAMHT (Rapid Acting Mental Health Treatment) and announces the next event, RAMHT-AI, for January 11, 2026.
statements.note: Own-event announcement; low forecast value. Coder may mark CONTROL.

statements.quote: One of the potential agents I’ve highlighted is the class of drugs called GLP-1 drugs—semeglutide, liguratide, tirzepetide, and more coming soon.
statements.context: Intro to the author's CNS Summit panel prep on GLP-1 receptor agonists for neuropsychiatric illness. He lists semaglutide, liraglutide and tirzepatide (author's spellings differ) and says more drugs in the class are coming soon.
statements.note: Pipeline call for the GLP-1 drug class; no company or product named for the coming drugs.

statements.quote: 20% of girls and 5% of boys will be sexually abused in childhood.
statements.context: Short post reacting to news about Jeffrey Epstein. The author restates, 'as I've written before', childhood sexual abuse prevalence figures in future tense.
statements.note: Prevalence statistic phrased as a future-tense base rate; borderline, truism-like. Author marks it as a restatement of an earlier claim.

statements.quote: I guess the internet shut down before I could solve this problem with one article. Bummer. I’m sure it will be working again in no time.
statements.context: Joke closing of the same short post (dated 2025-11-18): the article was cut off by an internet outage, and the author expects the internet to be working again shortly.
statements.note: Joke framing around an internet outage; the expectation of quick recovery reads as sincere. Low forecast value.

statements.quote: A live-action newsletter event coming up on January 11th in San Francisco: RAMHT 2026 SF.
statements.context: Podcast post on a German phase 3 trial of theta burst stimulation for auditory hallucinations. Closing announcement of the RAMHT 2026 SF live event on January 11 (2026) in San Francisco.
statements.note: Own-event announcement; restates the RAMHT date given in i-wrote-other-things-that-are-not. Coder may mark CONTROL.

statements.quote: Program Note! Our 5th live-action newsletter event is coming up on January 11th in San Francisco: RAMHT 2026 SF.
statements.context: Closing program note in a review of the AJP trial comparing DBT with SSRIs plus clinical management in borderline personality disorder. Fifth RAMHT live event scheduled for January 11 (2026) in San Francisco.
statements.note: Own-event announcement; third mention of this date in the packet. Coder may mark CONTROL.
